versions.shortDescription: Split two rows using a delimiter.
versions.longDescription:
# Transformer Combine Rows

Transformer Split Rows expands a CSV table by splitting delimited cell values into multiple rows.
It is the inverse operation of Transformer Combine Rows: instead of aggregating many rows into one,
it takes delimited values (e.g., "a,b,c") and normalizes them back into row-wise form. This is
useful when previously combined columns (codes/labels/IDs) must be processed as individual records
again.

## Core behavior

- Reads an input CSV table.
- If the first column is named id (case-insensitive), it is treated as an identifier column and is
  preserved.
- For every other column:
- values from all rows are converted to string form (implementation-dependent),
- then concatenated using the configured delimiter.
- Produces a single-row output CSV.

## Hyperparameter

- delimiter (STRING): Separator used when concatenating values (e.g., ",", ";", "|", "\n").

## Input

- table (CSV, required): Tabular input whose rows will be combined.

## Output

- combined (CSV): One-row table containing concatenated column values.

## Notes / assumptions

- Null/empty handling depends on the implementation (e.g., whether NaNs become empty strings or "
  nan").
- Non-string values are typically stringified before concatenation.
